_comment: Composite indexes for the leaderboards. Declared here so they are visible
from the source tree — the same reason firestore.rules is a file rather
than something that only exists in a console. Apply with
`bash scripts/deploy-indexes.sh`, which is NOT run by this repo's CI.
Firestore creates single-field indexes automatically, so the all-time
board (order by `best`) needs nothing here. A composite index is required
the moment a query combines an equality filter with an order-by on a
different field, which is exactly the shape of every windowed board:
Both directions per window, because direction is a property of the UNIT and
the catalog has both: points ranks high, while ms and moves rank low. An
index built in only one direction would make half the games' boards fail at
runtime rather than at deploy — and fail with a 400 that reads like a bug in
queryScope COLLECTION (not COLLECTION_GROUP): every board is queried on its
own path, `boards/<game>__<difficulty>/scores`. A COLLECTION-scoped index on
the `scores` collection id covers all of them at once, so adding a game
